about.description: Component TARA for the import example (0.19): the smoke detector case with its sensor chip (SDS). The external entity "Smoke Detector Controller" is the device it is built into; "Debugger" is the service access.

properties.description: Raw and filtered smoke measurement values of the optical chamber.

securityGoals.rationale: Smoke measurement values are not secret; reading them gives an attacker nothing.
Because when it is not available it is critical.

properties.description: Calibration parameters of the optical chamber (thresholds, drift compensation).
Firmware image of the sensor chip, signed by the manufacturer.
Detects smoke and reports it to the controller.

assumptions.text: The detector is mounted so that its debug connector cannot be reached without opening the housing; only service staff of the integrator open it.
The controller the detector is built into authenticates itself on the sensor link and keeps the link token secret.

threats.attackDescription: Attacker sets up a rogue endpoint pretending to be Sensor Diagnostic Controller, causing Debugger to send sensitive data to the attacker
threats.causeDescription: Missing endpoint validation before data transmission — Debugger cannot verify the true identity of the receiving endpoint
threats.threatDescription: Receiver spoofing: Attacker impersonates Sensor Diagnostic Controller to intercept data from Debugger

threats.attackDescription: Attacker intercepts the response from Sensor Diagnostic Controller and modifies data, causing Debugger to process falsified information
threats.causeDescription: Missing integrity protection on the response flow from Sensor Diagnostic Controller — Debugger cannot detect modified responses
threats.threatDescription: Response tampering: Attacker modifies response data before it reaches Debugger

threats.attackDescription: Sensor Diagnostic Controller claims it never received the data from Debugger, or denies having processed it
threats.causeDescription: No delivery confirmation or cryptographic receipt — Debugger has no proof that Sensor Diagnostic Controller received its data
threats.threatDescription: Receiver repudiation: Sensor Diagnostic Controller denies receiving or processing the request

threats.attackDescription: Attacker intercepts the response from Sensor Diagnostic Controller to Debugger and reads sensitive information
threats.causeDescription: Unencrypted or weakly protected response channel — response data is readable in transit
threats.threatDescription: Eavesdropping on response: Attacker intercepts sensitive response data from Sensor Diagnostic Controller

threats.attackDescription: Attacker disrupts or delays the response channel from Sensor Diagnostic Controller, causing Debugger to stall or fail
threats.causeDescription: No redundancy or timeout protection — Debugger depends on responses from Sensor Diagnostic Controller to continue operation
threats.threatDescription: Response blocking: Attacker prevents Debugger from receiving responses from Sensor Diagnostic Controller

threats.attackDescription: Attacker modifies the response from Sensor Diagnostic Controller to include elevated roles or permissions, causing Debugger to grant unauthorized access
threats.causeDescription: Debugger trusts response data from Sensor Diagnostic Controller without integrity verification, enabling privilege decisions based on forged responses
threats.threatDescription: Response manipulation for privilege escalation: Attacker manipulates response to gain elevated access in Debugger

threats.attackDescription: Attacker forges the identity of Debugger and sends malicious data to Sensor Diagnostic Controller, which processes it as legitimate
threats.causeDescription: Missing sender authentication on incoming data flow — Sensor Diagnostic Controller cannot verify the true origin of received data
threats.threatDescription: Sender spoofing: Attacker impersonates Debugger to deceive Sensor Diagnostic Controller

threats.attackDescription: Attacker attaches a hardware probe to the embedded bus and injects or modifies data packets
threats.causeDescription: Embedded bus carries no integrity protection or authentication — data is transmitted in plaintext
threats.threatDescription: Data tampering on embedded bus DF-8 between Debugger and Sensor Diagnostic Controller

threats.attackDescription: Debugger claims it never sent the command or data that Sensor Diagnostic Controller received and acted upon
threats.causeDescription: No non-repudiation mechanism on the data flow — requests from Debugger are not signed or cryptographically bound to the sender
threats.threatDescription: Sender repudiation: Debugger denies sending the request or data

threats.attackDescription: Attacker attaches a logic analyzer to the embedded bus and captures all traffic
threats.causeDescription: Embedded bus communication is unencrypted and physically accessible — data can be passively captured
threats.threatDescription: Eavesdropping on embedded bus DF-8 between Debugger and Sensor Diagnostic Controller

threats.attackDescription: Attacker sends a high volume of requests via the data flow, exhausting the processing capacity of Sensor Diagnostic Controller
threats.causeDescription: No rate limiting or request throttling protecting Sensor Diagnostic Controller from high-volume input via Debugger
threats.threatDescription: Request flooding: Attacker overwhelms Sensor Diagnostic Controller with excessive incoming requests

threats.attackDescription: Attacker uses the DF-8 interface to halt the processor, reads security keys and modifies execution flow to bypass access controls
threats.causeDescription: JTAG or SWD interface provides full processor access — attacker can halt CPU and modify execution flow
threats.threatDescription: Privilege escalation via DF-8 debug interface on Sensor Diagnostic Controller

threats.attackDescription: Attacker connects a rogue device to the interface and impersonates a legitimate system, gaining unauthorized access
threats.causeDescription: No hardware authentication on the interface — any device connecting is trusted without verification
threats.threatDescription: Interface identity spoofing — attacker impersonates a legitimate device on the interface

threats.attackDescription: Attacker modifies the interface hardware or firmware to intercept, inject, or block communications
threats.causeDescription: Interface lacks tamper detection and physical protection — unauthorized modification is possible without detection
threats.threatDescription: Interface tampering — attacker physically or logically tampers with the interface

threats.attackDescription: Attacker connects to the physical interface and denies having accessed it because no log record exists
threats.causeDescription: No logging of physical interface connections — who connected and when is unknown
threats.threatDescription: Interface access repudiation — physical interface access cannot be attributed

threats.attackDescription: Attacker attaches monitoring equipment to the physical interface and captures transmitted data
threats.causeDescription: Physical interface transmits data without encryption — signals are readable with basic test equipment
threats.threatDescription: Interface eavesdropping — attacker intercepts data on the physical interface

threats.threatDescription: Interface denial of service — attacker renders the interface unavailable
